audit_findings.title: Financial Services earnings may be capitalized without deducting required lending reinvestment
audit_findings.magnitude: unquantified (filed net finance-receivable additions were $24.7m in 2025; computed 2023-2025 average was $116.1m)
audit_findings.mechanism: OE—required equity-funded maintenance or growth investment in the lending portfolio would reduce distributable owner earnings
audit_findings.evidence: Net cash used by investing activities of $73.1 million in 2025 included additions to finance receivables of $913.6 million, which were partially offset by collections of $888.9 million.
audit_findings.explanation: The filing demonstrates that finance-receivable cash flows occur outside operating cash flow, but it does not demonstrate whether the $811.0m anchor deducted the required investment or what portion must be funded by common equity rather than borrowings. The three-year average net addition equals 14.3% of the anchor and, if representative and omitted, corresponds to about $31.01 per share of base value. This is reasonably capable of materially changing the valuation, although omission remains an unresolved possibility rather than a demonstrated calculation error.
audit_findings.action: Trace the 2026 OE reconciliation; calculate through-cycle changes in finance and contract receivables, associated debt funding and required equity capital; verify the normalized maintenance amount is deducted exactly once; then rerun all scenarios.

audit_findings.title: The bridge may treat operating and lending liquidity as wholly excess cash
audit_findings.magnitude: unquantified (maximum challenged bridge amount: $1,644.7m, or $31.26 per share and 12.6% of base equity value)
audit_findings.mechanism: bridge—cash that is required for operations, lending, regulation or taxes should not be added as a separable equity asset
audit_findings.evidence: The financing needs of Financial Services are met through intersegment borrowings and cash generated from Operations; Financial Services is charged interest expense on intersegment borrowings at market rates.
audit_findings.explanation: The valuation adds the entire $1,644.7m balance. The filing shows $1,644.2m is held in Operations rather than Financial Services, but Financial Services is funded through Operations and intersegment borrowing; it also identifies $580.2m held abroad for working capital, regulatory requirements or expansion. The record therefore does not establish how much is distributable excess cash. Because the challenged addition is $31.26 per share, determining even a substantial fraction to be required liquidity would materially lower the bridge and valuation.
audit_findings.action: Prepare a legal-entity liquidity schedule covering minimum operating cash, Financial Services funding and capital needs, the March 2027 debt repayment, restricted or regulatory cash, foreign withholding and repatriation taxes; rerun the bridge using only demonstrated distributable excess cash.

audit_findings.title: Recurring capitalized software development may have been stripped through the amortization add-back
audit_findings.magnitude: unquantified (filed 2025 additions: $18.9m; conservative computed base-value ceiling: $5.05 per share)
audit_findings.mechanism: OE—omitted software-development cash expenditure or an unsupported amortization add-back would overstate the anchor
audit_findings.evidence: During 2025, 2024 and 2023, Snap-on capitalized $ 18.9 million, $ 13.3 million and $ 11.0 million, respectively, of such costs.
audit_findings.explanation: Whether the reconciliation omitted these expenditures is unresolved. Nevertheless, the entire filed 2025 addition was only 2.3% of the $811.0m anchor. Treating all $18.9m as a recurring omitted deduction gives a conservative base-value effect of about $5.05 per share, leaving base value near $242.80 versus the $383 market price. The issue is therefore not capable on the supplied scale of changing the valuation conclusion.
audit_findings.action: Check whether capitalized software additions are included in maintenance reinvestment and whether the $11.6m 2025 software amortization was added back; correct any mismatch, but no conclusion-changing rerun is indicated unless broader omitted software costs are documented.

audit_findings.title: The latest anchor may retain a nonrecurring legal-settlement gain
audit_findings.magnitude: up to $16.2m after tax; computed base-value effect $4.33 per share
audit_findings.mechanism: OE—a retained one-time gain would inflate the anchor and every forecast year derived from it
audit_findings.evidence: The accompanying Consolidated Statements of Earnings for the year ended January 3, 2026, include a benefit in “Operating expenses” of $ 22.0 million for the settlement of a legal matter (the “2025 legal settlement”).
